headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: next-ai-draw-io’s broad browser/MCP egress can expose cognee’s sensitive support data if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can use browsers and MCP, so it may ingest content from cognee outputs if those are copied into files or prompts; cognee handles documents and workflows, creating a plausible instruction-injection bridge. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts or files, injected instructions can be executed.
IF both agents share an MCP server or clipboard bridge, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of untrusted agent output into prompts.
Use a read-only export format between agents.
Add a provenance banner to all imported text.
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted actions.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and multiple third-party API options. If the pair shares files or prompts, sensitive content can leave the local boundary through next-ai-draw-io’s backend calls. The interaction is inferred, but the blast radius is clearly sensitive and potentially exfiltrative.
conditions: IF cognee data is forwarded into next-ai-draw-io prompts or uploads, sensitive records may be transmitted to external APIs.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace, file contents can leak through next-ai-draw-io network calls.
mitigations: Keep sensitive cognee data out of next-ai-draw-io inputs.
Route next-ai-draw-io through a local-only model.
Separate workspaces and credentials per agent.
Turn off external API providers in next-ai-draw-io.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress controls at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and cognee has session memory while next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and broad egress. If they are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared resources, concurrent writes or conflicting tool actions are plausible. No locking is documented, so the safest choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or diagram file, edits can collide.
IF an MCP tool mutates shared state without locks, concurrent actions can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Use read-only mode for one agent during the other’s write phase.
Back up files before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io is designed for AI-assisted visualization and natural-language commands, so it may treat cognee’s generated workflows or decisions as authoritative input. cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which can be rendered or acted on downstream without verification. That creates a strong cascade path from generated content to incorrect artifacts or actions.
conditions: IF cognee output is imported into next-ai-draw-io without review, errors can propagate into diagrams or actions.
IF next-ai-draw-io auto-applies suggested changes, downstream mistakes become user-visible artifacts.
mitigations: Require human review before applying imported content.
Mark cognee output as untrusted by default.
Use a diff view instead of auto-apply.
Limit next-ai-draw-io to visualization-only mode.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking step.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while next-ai-draw-io handles documents and uses external AI providers with API keys. If regulated data is routed through those providers, retention or residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data is sent to a third-party model provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, external API routing can violate them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external model calls.
Use a provider with an approved DPA.
Disable logging for sensitive sessions.
Review retention settings before processing.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
